roots.label: arts, culture, entertainment and media
roots.description: All forms of arts, entertainment, cultural heritage and media

children.label: arts and entertainment
children.description: All forms of arts and entertainment

children.label: animation
children.description: Stories told through animated drawings in either full-length or short format

children.label: cartoon
children.description: Drawings, such as editorial cartoons and comic strips, often using humor or satire

children.label: movies
children.description: Stories told through motion pictures, such as full-length or short format documentary or fictional features

children.label: dance
children.description: A form of performing art consisting of purposefully selected sequences of human movement

children.label: ballet
children.description: A classical dance form based on formal gestures, steps and postures

children.label: modern dance
children.description: A theatrical dance style based on free-style expression rather than formal gestures

children.label: traditional dance
children.description: Dance style that reflects the life and culture of a specific group of people or region, such as folk and ceremonial dance

children.label: fashion
children.description: Styles and trends in clothing, footwear, accessories, including the design, presentation and wearing of these styles and trends

children.label: cosmetics
children.description: Products applied to the body to enhance appearance, such as lipstick, eyeliner, foundation and nail polish, and the trends surrounding the application of these products

children.label: hairstyles
children.description: Trends surrounding the cutting and styling of hair

children.label: jewelry
children.description: Decorative items worn for personal expression and adornment, such as rings, necklaces, earrings

children.label: festival
children.description: Events showcasing artistic endeavors, often regularly occurring, such as dance, music, theater, poetry or comedy festivals

children.label: film festival
children.description: All forms of national and international film festivals

children.label: literature
children.description: The telling of a story through written language

children.label: drama (literature)
children.description: Work written to be performed on the stage

children.label: fiction
children.description: Written works that are not based on fact, but are the creation of the author's imagination

children.label: non-fiction
children.description: Written works that are based on fact

children.label: poetry
children.description: Written works that use the esthetic and rhythmic qualities of language to express a message or emotion

children.label: music
children.description: A form of performing art using instruments or voice to create different sounds, tones and harmonies

children.label: musical genre
children.description: A distinguishable type of music

children.label: children's music
children.description: A genre of music featuring songs composed and performed for children

children.label: classical music
children.description: A genre of music rooted in the traditions of Western music, including both religious and secular music, such as symphony, concerto and sonata.

children.label: country music
children.description: A genre of music that originated in the southern United States, often consisting of ballads or dance tunes and featuring string instruments such as banjos, fiddles and guitars

children.label: dance band music
children.description: A Swedish genre of music characterized by music inspired by swing, schlager, country, jazz and rock that is often danced to in pairs

children.label: electronic dance music
children.description: A genre of music that employs electronic instruments and is primarily made for nightclubs, raves, and festivals

children.label: folk music
children.description: A genre of music that developed from traditional popular cultures, often based on story telling

children.label: heavy metal
children.description: A genre of loud, aggressive rock music that was developed in the late 1960s and early 1970s

children.label: hip hop
children.description: A genre of music developed in African American communities in the United States in the 1970s which consists of rapping usually with an electronic backing

children.label: jazz music
children.description: A genre of music with roots in blues and ragtime that originated in African American communities of New Orleans in the United States in the late 19th and early 20th centuries

children.label: popular music
children.description: A genre of music that is widely accessible and designed to appeal to all

children.label: r&b
children.description: A genre of music originated in African American communities in the 1940s and featuring soulful vocals

children.label: rock and roll music
children.description: A genre of music that originated in the United States during the late 1940s and early 1950s, evolving from African American musical styles such as gospel, jump blues, jazz, boogie woogie, and rhythm and blues.

children.label: musical instrument
children.description: Objects used to play music on

children.label: musical performance
children.description: Musicians performing for an audience for the purpose of entertainment

children.label: series
children.description: A connected set of fictional or non-fictional program episodes that run under the same title.

children.label: theater
children.description: A form of performing art where live performers portray a narrative to an audience through dialog and action

children.label: cabaret
children.description: A form of theatrical entertainment featuring music, song, dance, recitation, or drama that is performed in a nightclub or restaurant while the audience eats or drinks at tables

children.label: drama (theatre)
children.description: A genre of theatre where dramatic or comedic plays are performed on the stage

children.label: musical
children.description: A genre of music theatre in which singing and dancing play an essential part of the storytelling

children.label: opera
children.description: A form of performing art where classically trained musicians and singers perform a musical and dramatic work

children.label: operetta
children.description: A genre of music theatre that usually has a light or humorous theme where some of the libretto is usually spoken rather than sung.

children.label: stand-up comedy
children.description: A comic style in which a comedian performs a series of jokes or stories in front of a live audience, usually speaking directly to them

children.label: visual arts
children.description: A form of art which appeals primarily to the visual senses, such as ceramics, drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, design, crafts, photography, video, filmmaking, and architecture.

children.label: architecture
children.description: The design of buildings, monuments and the spaces around them

children.label: design (visual arts)
children.description: An artistic discipline which focuses on visual communication and presentation, the final product of which can range from jewelry to interior design

children.label: drawing
children.description: A form of visual arts using mediums such as pencils, markers, pen and ink, charcoal

children.label: forging
children.description: The shaping of metal using localized compressive forces, such as heating and hammering

children.label: painting
children.description: A form of visual arts using mediums such as oil paint, watercolor, pastel, crayon

children.label: photography
children.description: A form of visual arts using photographic images

children.label: sculpture
children.description: A form of visual arts using mediums such as clay, stone, wood and metal to create three-dimensional works

children.label: textile arts
children.description: Arts and crafts that use plant, animal, or synthetic fibres to construct practical or decorative object

children.label: woodworking
children.description: The activity or skill of making items, such as furniture or cabinets, from wood

children.label: culture
children.description: The ideas, customs, arts, traditions of a particular group of persons

children.label: art exhibition
children.description: Temporary presentation of art in museums, art halls or galleries

children.label: cultural development
children.description: The history of the development of art and culture such as the rise of cave paintings, linguistic variations over time, the evolution of values

children.label: customs and tradition
children.description: A particular way of behaving, or observances that have developed over time by a group of people

children.label: festive event (culture)
children.description: An event ordinarily celebrated by a community and centering on some characteristic aspect of that community and its religion or traditions

children.label: language
children.description: The method of human communication, either spoken or written, consisting of words that are used in a structured and conventional way

children.label: library and museum
children.description: Institutions that house collections of books, music, art, or objects from the past and present optionally for public use and display

children.label: monument and heritage site
children.description: Commemorations of historical people, events, or the areas containing them, in the form of structures such as sculptures, statues or buildings

children.label: restoration
children.description: Restoring historic or important properties or structures to a former better state by cleaning, repairing or rebuilding

children.label: mass media
children.description: Media addressing a large audience

children.label: disinformation and misinformation
children.description: The spread of false information regardless of intent

children.label: news media
children.description: The presentation of news to the public through different platforms, such as TV, radio, newspapers, magazines, web pages and blogs

children.label: newspaper
children.description: Daily or weekly publication that presents the news, locally, regionally or globally, as well as features, opinion columns, comics and other content

children.label: online media outlet
children.description: Publication distributing content, such as articles, blogs, photos, video and music, only over the internet

children.label: periodical
children.description: Publication that is usually published weekly, bi-weekly, monthly or annually, such as magazines, journals or newsletters

children.label: radio
children.description: Audio content, such as news, entertainment or information, distributed via broadcast or internet

children.label: social media
children.description: Content created to be shared within online social networks

children.label: influencers
children.description: Persons who distribute content on internet forums and social media and are followed by many people thereby influencing them to buy and use products

children.label: television
children.description: Video content, such as news, entertainment or information, distributed via broadcast or internet

roots.label: conflict, war and peace
roots.description: Acts of socially or politically motivated protest or violence, military activities, geopolitical conflicts, as well as resolution efforts

children.label: act of terror
children.description: Act of violence, often resulting in casualties, designed to raise fear and anxiety in a population

children.label: act of bioterrorism
children.description: Attacks using biological agents intended to raise the level of fear within a population

children.label: terrorist bombings
children.description: Intentional use of explosive devices on people, buildings or other structures

children.label: armed conflict
children.description: Disputes between opposing groups involving the use of weapons, but not necessarily formally declared wars

children.label: guerrilla activity
children.description: Anti-government or wartime actions by clandestine or non-state combatant groups, often using tactics such as ambush, sabotage, raids and kidnapping

children.label: international military intervention
children.description: The temporary use of international forces in a country or region that requires outside help with resolving a crisis

children.label: military occupation
children.description: The temporary forceful taking over of a country or region by invading military forces

children.label: war
children.description: Armed hostilities by one group or geopolitical entity against another

children.label: civil war
children.description: Armed conflict between members of the same country, in some cases with the goal of dividing the country

children.label: civil unrest
children.description: Rallies, strikes, demonstrations, riots or other disturbances by a population, often in protest to a government or other organization's policies or actions

children.label: protests and demonstrations
children.description: A non-violent public show of support for or opposition to a cause, idea or policy, in the form of a mass meeting or march

children.label: rebellion
children.description: Organized actions of opposition to a government or ruling party by a country's residents, often violent and with the aim of overthrowing the government

children.label: revolution
children.description: A forcible and often violent change to, or overthrow of, a country's political system or social order by internal forces, in favor of a new system

children.label: riot
children.description: Violent, destructive events of civil disorder by groups of people, usually in response to a grievance or as acts of opposition, often involving injury to individuals and destruction of property

children.label: coup d'etat
children.description: The overthrow of an established government by an organized military or political group

children.label: cyber warfare
children.description: Cyber attacks, or suspected attacks, involving a government entity as either the sponsor or the target, or preventive measures against these types of actions

children.label: massacre
children.description: The mass killing of people, usually civilians, during wartime hostilities

children.label: peace process
children.description: Organized actions to end a war or conflict, usually involving peace negotiations and agreements

children.label: disarmament
children.description: The abolishment or reduction of a country's military weapons cache

children.label: peace envoy
children.description: Person or organization initiating and carrying out a peace process

children.label: peace plan
children.description: A strategy for achieving peace in a warring nation or area of conflict

children.label: peace talks
children.description: Discussions between countries, world regions or geopolitical entities in conflict or at war, often with a mediator, with the goal of arriving at a solution for peace

children.label: peacekeeping force
children.description: The military forces of a nation, or of several nations working together, whose mission is to maintain peace in areas of conflict

children.label: post-war reconstruction
children.description: Actions to rebuild a society, economy or political system in an area affected by war

children.label: ordnance clearance
children.description: The removal or neutralization of ordnance such as landmines or cluster bombs that may remain after a war or armed conflict on public ground

children.label: war victims
children.description: Individuals who are injured or killed in a war or armed conflict, including civilians

children.label: missing in action
children.description: Civilians or military personnel who have gone missing during or after hostilities, conflicts or war

children.label: prisoners of war
children.description: Individuals captured, imprisoned or detained by enemy factions during military conflicts or war

roots.label: crime, law and justice
roots.description: The establishment and/or statement of the rules of behavior in society, the enforcement of these rules, breaches of the rules, the punishment of offenders and the organizations and bodies involved in these activities

children.label: crime
children.description: Violations of laws by individuals, companies or organizations

children.label: animal abuse
children.description: The infliction of cruelty or neglect onto animals by humans

children.label: arson
children.description: The intentional setting of fires with criminal intent

children.label: assault
children.description: Physical crime against a person, including battery, brawls and threat of bodily harm

children.label: sex crime
children.description: Sexual crimes against a person, such as rape, harassment, molestation or groping

children.label: corporate crime
children.description: Crimes committed by a corporation or by individuals acting on behalf of a corporation

children.label: accounting crime
children.description: The intentional misrepresentation or alteration of accounting records regarding sales, revenues, expenses and other factors

children.label: anti-trust crime
children.description: Violations of laws aimed at corporations to promote fair competition for the benefit of consumers

children.label: breach of contract
children.description: The breaking of terms set in a contractual agreement

children.label: embezzlement
children.description: The intentional theft or misuse of money left in one's care or belonging to one's employer

children.label: insider trading
children.description: Trading of stocks by persons having access to internal information not made public at the time

children.label: restraint of trade
children.description: Interference in free competition in business and trade

children.label: corruption
children.description: Dishonest actions by a person in power in return for pecuniary or personal gain

children.label: bribery
children.description: The giving of money or favors in order to influence the judgment or conduct of a person in a position of power

children.label: cyber crime
children.description: Criminal activities carried out by means of computers or the internet, such as hacking, phishing scams and identity theft

children.label: drug related crimes
children.description: Illegal activities involving illicit substances, including buying, distribution, selling and smuggling

children.label: drug trafficking
children.description: Dealing in illicit often harmful substances

children.label: fraud
children.description: Intentional deception for personal or financial gain

children.label: tax evasion
children.description: The illegal evasion of taxes by individuals, corporations, and trusts

children.label: genocide
children.description: The systematic killing of one clan, tribe, or religious or ethnic group by another

children.label: hijacking
children.description: Taking over a transportation vehicle by force

children.label: homicide
children.description: The killing of one person by another, including murder and manslaughter

children.label: human smuggling and trafficking
children.description: The illegal transporting of people from one country or area to another. When the result is forced labor or sexual exploitation, the crime is considered trafficking.

children.label: kidnapping
children.description: To seize and detain a person against that person's will by unlawful threat, force or fraud

children.label: organized crime
children.description: Crimes committed by gangs or criminal organizations, such as the mafia

children.label: gang activity
children.description: Criminal activities by groups of individuals, who are allied by common territories, languages or ethnic backgrounds and identify by a common group identity by using a shared name, tattoo, hand sign, clothing style or graffiti symbol

children.label: reckless driving
children.description: Serious traffic violations that are likely to, or have led to, the endangerment, injury or death of a person or persons, or the endangerment of or significant property damage

children.label: robbery and theft
children.description: The taking of another person's property without their consent, sometimes by force

children.label: shootings
children.description: An act of violence committed by individuals with the use of armed weapons

children.label: terrorism
children.description: Violence against people to create fear in order to achieve political or ideological objectives

children.label: torture
children.description: Intentionally inflicting severe physical or psychological pain in order to punish the victim or get the victim to take an action or give information

children.label: vandalism
children.description: Deliberately damaging or destroying public or private property

children.label: war crime
children.description: Crimes committed during a war or armed conflict, usually against civilians or prisoners of war, including the prosecution of such crimes

children.label: judiciary
children.description: The system of courts of law

children.label: court
children.description: Place where legal cases are heard and decided

children.label: appeal (court)
children.description: Process in which parties request a formal change to an official decision

children.label: judge
children.description: Official who decides cases in a court of law and passes sentences on those found guilty

children.label: supreme and high court
children.description: matters related to supreme or high courts, including nominations and rulings

children.label: trial (court)
children.description: The process by which evidence is presented and guilt, innocence or culpability is determined

children.label: litigation
children.description: Taking disputed issues to court for settlement by judge and/or jury

children.label: pre-trial
children.description: Actions that happen before the start of a trial, such as pleas, bail motions, discovery and depositions

children.label: sentencing (criminal)
children.description: The retribution handed out to those who break laws

children.label: capital punishment
children.description: The legally authorized execution of someone as punishment for a crime

children.label: court-ordered psychiatric treatment
children.description: Psychiatric treatment imposed upon persons with mental health conditions in prisons and jails or as a condition of probation, supervision or parole

children.label: fine (penalty)
children.description: Money that a court of law or other authority decides has to be paid as punishment for a crime or other offence

children.label: prison
children.description: Facility where people are held as a punishment for a crime they have committed or while awaiting trial

children.label: suspended sentence
children.description: Legal arrangement where a judge delays the serving of a sentence by a person who has been found guilty of a crime in order to give them a probationary period

children.label: out of court procedures
children.description: Legal issues which are settled outside of court

children.label: arbitration and mediation
children.description: Resolution of disputed issues by a neutral panel, including conciliation, negotiation and tribunals

children.label: prosecution and prosecutors
children.description: The process of holding a trial against a person or entity who is accused of a crime to determine guilt and the lawyers and legal team who argue that the accused is guilty

children.label: law
children.description: The codification of rules of behavior

children.label: administrative law
children.description: Body of law that governs the actions of governmental administrative agencies

children.label: civil law
children.description: The system of law focused on private rights and disputes between individuals in such areas as contracts, torts, property, and family law

children.label: regulations
children.description: laws that guide the conduct and organization of business corporations

children.label: antitrust regulations
children.description: laws to promote competition between companies for the benefit of consumers

children.label: criminal law
children.description: The system of law concerned with the punishment of those who commit crimes

children.label: international law
children.description: The system of laws embraced by all nations, such as the Geneva Convention and the International Law of the Seas

children.label: extradition
children.description: Legal transfer of criminals or suspects between countries

children.label: international court and tribunal
children.description: The activities of courts under the authority of international organizations or formed by treaties between nations, such as the European Court for Human Rights and International Court of Justice

children.label: law enforcement
children.description: Agencies that attempt to prevent disobedience to established laws or bring to justice those who disobey those laws

children.label: arrest
children.description: The detention of a suspect of a crime

children.label: investigation (criminal)
children.description: Inquiry into an alleged crime, including searching, interviews, interrogations and evidence collection

children.label: dropped criminal investigation
children.description: When police and/or prosecutors end an investigation without a conclusion

children.label: missing person
children.description: An adult whose disappearance is possibly not voluntary, or a child whose whereabouts are unknown to the child's legal guardian

children.label: police
children.description: Civil force of a national, regional or local government that is responsible for the prevention and detection of crime and the maintenance of public order

children.label: surveillance
children.description: Monitoring the activities of the individual through the use of cameras and data in order to prevent or uncover criminal activities

roots.label: disaster, accident and emergency incident
roots.description: Man made or natural event resulting in loss of life or injury to living creatures and/or damage to inanimate objects or property

children.label: accident and emergency incident
children.description: A sudden, unexpected event that causes unwanted consequences or requires immediate action

children.label: drowning
children.description: When a person's airpipe and lungs become filled with water causing death or injury, most often caused by falling into or bathing in rivers, lakes or the ocean

children.label: explosion accident and incident
children.description: Explosions caused by an accidental, non-combat, or non-terrorism source. Also use when the source of the explosion is non-specified or unknown

children.label: industrial accident and incident
children.description: Any unplanned event or mishap in an industrial setting that result in injuries to people and damage to property or the environment

children.label: nuclear accident and incident
children.description: Any unplanned event that causes unwanted consequences involving radioactive materials

children.label: structural failure
children.description: The unexpected collapse of a building, bridge or other structure

children.label: transportation accident and incident
children.description: An accident or incident involving one or more vehicles

children.label: air and space accident and incident

value.label: air and space accident and incident

children.description: An accident or incident involving aircrafts or spacecrafts

children.label: maritime accident and incident
children.description: An accident or incident involving marine vessels.

children.label: railway accident and incident
children.description: An accident or incident involving trains.

children.label: road accident and incident
children.description: An accident or incident involving road vehicles.

children.label: wildlife traffic accident
children.description: Traffic accidents involving wild animals

children.label: disaster
children.description: A sudden, unplanned event that causes great damage or loss of life, such as an accident or a natural catastrophe

children.label: famine
children.description: Severe lack of food for a large population

children.label: fire
children.description: Fires started by an accidental or unknown source. For wildfires, use wildfire. For fires started with a criminal intent, use arson.

children.label: wildfire
children.description: An uncontrolled fire in an area of combustible vegetation

children.label: natural disaster
children.description: Destructive incidents caused by nature, such as earthquakes and floods

children.label: drought
children.description: A severe lack of water over a period of time

children.label: earthquake
children.description: The shifting of the tectonic plates of the Earth, creating in some cases damage to structures

children.label: flood
children.description: Surfeit of water, caused by heavy rains or melting snow, usually in places where it's not wanted

children.label: landslide
children.description: Sudden dislodging of massive amounts of snow or soil

children.label: avalanche
children.description: A sudden fall of snow, ice, rock, or mud down the side of a mountain

children.label: meteorological disaster
children.description: A weather-related disaster

children.label: hurricane
children.description: A type of storm also called a tropical cyclone, which forms over tropical or subtropical waters

children.label: windstorms
children.description: A storm with very strong wind but little or no rain or snow

children.label: tsunami
children.description: High and powerful ocean waves caused by an underwater land disturbance, such as an earthquake or volcanic eruption, known to cause significant damage and loss when they hit land

children.label: volcanic eruption
children.description: A rupture in the crust of the Earth allowing molten material to escape to the surface

children.label: emergency response
children.description: The planning and efforts made by people and organizations to help victims of a sudden, unplanned event, natural disaster or crisis

roots.label: economy, business and finance
roots.description: All matters concerning the planning, production and exchange of wealth.

children.label: business enterprise
children.description: Organizations set up to create and sell a product or service

children.label: cooperative
children.description: An organization which is owned and run jointly by its members, who share the profits or benefits of their work

children.label: small and medium enterprise
children.description: A small and medium enterprise (SME) is a company whose number of employees, balance and turnover cannot exceed certain limits set by the country where it is located

children.label: start-up and entrepreneurial business
children.description: The process of designing, launching and running a new business

children.label: business information
children.description: Information about individual business entities, including companies, corporations, charities

children.label: business financing
children.description: The financing, capital structuring, and investment decisions of a business

children.label: bankruptcy
children.description: News about actual bankruptcy filings.

children.label: corporate bond
children.description: Corporate paper representing the loan of money at a fixed rate and for a fixed time to that company or government

children.label: crowdfunding
children.description: The funding of a project or venture by raising small amounts of money from a large number of people, typically via the internet

children.label: financially distressed company
children.description: Indications that a company is financially distressed but not having filed for bankruptcy yet

children.label: stocks and securities
children.description: Financial instruments such as company shares and bonds

children.label: corporate dividends
children.description: Distribution of company profits to shareholders via dividend payments

children.label: derivatives
children.description: Financial instruments such as futures, swaps and options that depend on an underlying instrument such as a commodity, bond, equity or currency

children.label: stock activity
children.description: Announcements of major stock events: splits, block trades, new highs or lows, etc.

children.label: stock buyback
children.description: Corporate actions in which companies buy back their own shares

children.label: stock flotation
children.description: The issuing of stock shares to the public for the first time, also called an Initial Public Offering (IPO)

children.label: business governance
children.description: The rules, practices, and processes used to oversee and manage a company

children.label: annual and special corporate meeting
children.description: News surrounding company reports and annual or special corporate meetings

children.label: annual report
children.description: Availability or contents of annual company reports.

children.label: board of directors
children.description: Appointments to or changes in the board of directors for a company.

children.label: environmental, social and governance policy (ESG)
children.description: A company's business practices reflecting responsible social, ethical and environmental policies, sometimes known as corporate social responsibility

children.label: proxy filing
children.description: Filings with regulatory agencies of proxy statements for upcoming shareholder votes.

children.label: shareholder activity
children.description: Actions taken by owners of one or more shares of a company, including shareholder activism

children.label: business reporting and performance
children.description: Measuring and reporting on the performance of a business

children.label: corporate earnings
children.description: Announcements and discussions of corporate earnings

children.label: credit rating
children.description: Formal statements by certain rating agencies on the investment risk of a company or enterprise

children.label: financial statement
children.description: Formal statements about the company financials typically delivered annually or quarterly

children.label: business restructuring
children.description: Changes to the structure of a business or organisation

children.label: company spin-off
children.description: The creation of new companies being spun off from existing companies.

children.label: joint venture
children.description: Two or more companies agreeing on a venture.

children.label: leveraged buyout
children.description: Acquiring control over a company by buying its shares with borrowed money.

children.label: management buyout
children.description: Acquiring control over a company by the management buying its shares.

children.label: merger or acquisition
children.description: Two or more companies forming a new company mergers, takeovers or acquisitions.

children.label: business strategy and marketing
children.description: Planning the direction of a company and selling its products and services to achieve the strategy

children.label: client relationship management
children.description: Creating and maintaining a relationship with the customers to increase sales.

children.label: commercial contract
children.description: Contracts regarding commercial activities

children.label: economic globalization
children.description: Doing business around the world

children.label: market research
children.description: Gathering information about the needs and wants of consumers

children.label: market trend
children.description: Statistically significant consumer behavior.

children.label: new product or service
children.description: The introduction of products or services to the market

children.label: outsourcing
children.description: Business practice in which services or job functions are farmed out to a third party

children.label: patent, copyright and trademark
children.description: Intellectual properties such as patents, copyright and trademarks

children.label: product recall
children.description: A decision by a company to take back or repair a defective product

children.label: public contract
children.description: Written contracts between companies and public authorities for the execution of works, the supply of products or the provision of services.

children.label: research and development
children.description: Research and expenditure on new product or service development

children.label: human resources
children.description: People working for a business and how they are managed

children.label: executive officer
children.description: Company executive officers including appointments and changes

children.label: layoffs and downsizing
children.description: Planned or actual reductions in the labor force.

children.label: economy
children.description: Production, consumption, distribution and trade activities affecting regions or countries as a whole

children.label: central bank
children.description: A country's major bank that sets interest rates and provides transfer of funds between commercial banks

children.label: currency
children.description: The system of money used by a country, including the value of one currency as measured against another

children.label: cryptocurrency
children.description: An internet-based medium of exchange using cryptography to conduct financial transactions

children.label: economic organization
children.description: Business, industrial and trade associations, societies and other private-sector groups

children.label: economic trends and indicators
children.description: The behavior and performance of the economy as a whole

children.label: consumer confidence
children.description: A measure of consumers' feelings about current and future economic conditions, including prices, inflation and the quality of retail goods, used as an indicator of the overall state of the economy

children.label: deflation
children.description: The decrease in the general price level of goods and services within an economy

children.label: economic growth
children.description: An increase of the gross domestic product (GDP)

children.label: employment statistics
children.description: Trends and statistics about areas such as job growth, unemployment and wage growth

children.label: exporting

children.label: parental leave
children.description: Time off work to give birth or care for a child

children.label: self-employment
children.description: A situation in which an individual works for themselves as a freelancer or business owner instead of working for an employer that pays a salary or a wage

children.label: volunteering
children.description: Unpaid work undertaken freely by individuals as a service to others

children.label: wages and benefits
children.description: Money, or other items of value such as pension contributions and health insurance, paid to employees as compensation for their work

children.label: profit sharing
children.description: A system by which employees are paid a share of the net profits of their employer. These earnings are distinct from and additional to regular wages.

children.label: social security
children.description: a government system that provides monetary assistance to people with inadequate or no incomes, such as retirees, disabled people or caregivers

children.label: employment legislation

children.label: workplace health and safety
children.description: Laws protecting a safe and healthy work environment

children.label: labor market
children.description: The supply and demand of labor in an economy

children.label: gig economy
children.description: a labor market consisting of individual suppliers on short-term contracts or freelance work as opposed to permanent jobs, such as drivers or delivery workers

children.label: labor relations
children.description: The relationship between workers and employers

children.label: collective agreements

children.label: labor dispute

children.label: labor strike
children.description: Groups of employees agreeing to cease work activities with the aim of achieving better pay or work conditions

children.label: retirement
children.description: The years after work

children.label: pension
children.description: Payments, either government or private, to retired people

children.label: unemployment
children.description: The state of being available to work but not having a job

children.label: unemployment benefits
children.description: Monetary compensation paid to the jobless

children.label: unions
children.description: Groups established to represent bodies of workers in order to obtain better workplace conditions through collective bargaining

roots.label: lifestyle and leisure
roots.description: Activities undertaken for pleasure, relaxation or recreation outside paid employment, including eating and travel.

children.label: leisure
children.description: Activities carried out in ones' spare time and not in a competitive way.

children.label: club and association
children.description: organizations joined by individuals because of similar interests

children.label: game
children.description: Contests generally for one's amusement

children.label: board game
children.description: A game played on a board

children.label: card game
children.description: A game played with a pack of cards

children.label: children's game
children.description: A game designed for and most often played by children

children.label: dice game
children.description: A game played using dice only

children.label: outdoor game
