children.label: puzzle
children.description: A game played solving logic problems for entertainment

children.label: tile game
children.description: A game played using tiles

children.label: video game
children.description: A game played using a video display

children.label: gaming and lottery
children.description: Gambling, often involving selection of sets of numbers one expects to come up

children.label: hobby
children.description: Recreational pursuit

children.label: automobile enthusiasm
children.description: Interest in new and classic cars

children.label: bicycle enthusiasm
children.description: Interest in new and classic manpowered cycles

children.label: collecting
children.description: The hobby of seeking, locating, acquiring, organizing, cataloging, displaying, storing or maintaining items that are of interest to an individual collector

children.label: food and drink enthusiasm
children.description: Interest in eating and drinking

children.label: beer, wine and spirits
children.description: Interest in the consumption, production and collection of alcoholic beverages

children.label: cooking and baking
children.description: Interest in preparing meals or baked goods

children.label: motorcycle enthusiasm
children.description: Interest in new and classic motor-powered cycles

children.label: vacation
children.description: Time spent not at work for rest and relaxation

children.label: Halloween
children.description: A celebration observed in a number of countries on 31 October with activities including trick-or-treating, wearing costumes, carving pumpkins, visiting haunted attractions, telling scary stories and watching horror films

children.label: public holiday
children.description: A day of celebration declared by a government

children.label: Midsummer
children.description: Northern European celebrations that accompany the Summer solstice

children.label: National day
children.description: A designated day to celebrate a nation

children.label: New year
children.description: The celebration of the end of one calendar year and the start of next

children.label: leisure venue
children.description: A place where people go to be entertained or amused

children.label: amusement park
children.description: A park providing various rides and entertainment attractions for both adults and children, including theme parks

children.label: bar
children.description: A business where drinks are prepared and served to the public for consumption on the premises

children.label: cafe
children.description: A small business where drinks and snacks are prepared and served - its specifics may depend on the local culture

children.label: nightclub
children.description: A commercial establishment providing music, or other entertainment along with food and drink to selected clientele

children.label: park and playground
children.description: A public green area in a town or city used for recreation

children.label: restaurant
children.description: A business where meals are prepared and served to the public

children.label: zoo
children.description: A park where visitors can see both wild and tame animals that are kept in cages or enclosed areas

children.label: outdoor recreational activities
children.description: Leisure activities engaged in the outdoors, most commonly in natural settings

children.label: fishing
children.description: A recreational activity involving the use of baits, lures, weapons and traps for the capture of aquatic species.

children.label: horseback riding
children.description: The riding of horses for leisure or light exercise.

children.label: hunting
children.description: An activity involving the use of weapons or traps for the capturing of animals

children.label: recreational hiking and climbing
children.description: Sportive activities in the mountains including climbing and hiking

children.label: scuba diving
children.description: Underwater diving with the use of a self-contained underwater breathing apparatus

children.label: travel and tourism
children.description: Spending time away from home in pursuit of recreation, relaxation or pleasure

children.label: lifestyle
children.description: The way in which a person lives, including their style and possessions

children.label: house and home
children.description: Interest in maintaining and decorating one's home

children.label: gardening
children.description: Interest in working in one's garden

children.label: home renovation
children.description: Interest in renovating one's property

children.label: interior decoration
children.description: Interest in decorating one's home

children.label: organic food
children.description: Food which is grown using no artificial fertilizers or chemical compounds

children.label: party
children.description: A social gathering of invited guests, often involving eating, drinking, dancing or the playing of games

children.label: trend
children.description: Interest in what is considered hip or popular at a certain point in time

children.label: body modification
children.description: Actions taken to permanently or semi-permanently change body appearance, such as piercing and tattooing

children.label: piercing
children.description: A form of body modification involving the puncturing or cutting of a part of the human body, creating an opening in which jewelry may be worn or where an implant could be inserted

children.label: tattooing
children.description: A form of body modification where a design is made by inserting ink, dyes and pigments into the dermis layer of the skin to permanently change the pigment

children.label: vegetarianism and veganism
children.description: The avoidance of meat and other animal products for moral, dietary or religious reasons and the plant-based products that adhere to this principle

children.label: wellness
children.description: The active pursuit of good mental and physical health

children.label: exercise and fitness
children.description: Physical activity with the purpose to maintain and improve health and wellness, gain stamina or for enjoyment

children.label: mental wellbeing
children.description: The personal pursuit of mental health through activities such as meditation, stress reduction, technology detoxes and journaling

roots.label: politics and government
roots.description: Local, regional, national and international exercise of power, the day-to-day running of government, and the relationships between governing bodies and states.

children.label: election
children.description: The selection of government representatives by the casting of votes by the populace

children.label: special election
children.description: An election used to fill an office that has become vacant between general elections because of the death of a politician, a resignation or other reason

children.label: campaign finance
children.description: The money that makes campaigns for public office possible

children.label: citizens' initiative and recall
children.description: Political suggestions by non-government officials for corrective action, or for changes in existing rules and regulations

children.label: coalition building
children.description: Political parties entering a power-sharing arrangement usually occurring when no single party has achieved an absolute majority after an election

children.label: intergovernmental elections
children.description: Choosing individuals for the leadership of an international organization, such as the United Nations, European Union, NATO and World Bank

children.label: local elections
children.description: Choosing individuals for government at the city, village or county level

children.label: national elections
children.description: Choosing individuals for government at a national level

children.label: political candidates
children.description: Individuals who are chosen to stand for office

children.label: political debates
children.description: Organized debates between political candidates during their election campaign

children.label: primary elections
children.description: Preliminary elections or caucuses to choose candidates to represent a political party in a regional or national election

children.label: recall election
children.description: A special election to vote to remove an elected official from office before that official's term has ended

children.label: referendum
children.description: Political proposals, laws and actions to be voted on by the entire voting body, including ballot measures and citizens' initiatives

children.label: state elections
children.description: Choosing individuals for government at a regional, state or province level

children.label: voting
children.description: The act of casting a ballot for a candidate, a party or an initiative in a political election, including voting machines, voting by mail or voter turnout

children.label: electoral system
children.description: The set of rules that determine how elections are conducted and how their results are determined, including discussions of the electoral college, ranked choice voting or the allocation of governmental seats

children.label: government
children.description: The systems, institutions and people who run a political entity

children.label: constitution (law)
children.description: A basic framework that stands above all laws and regulations, specifying how a particular political entity is governed

children.label: executive (government)
children.description: Branch of government that is responsible for implementing the laws passed by the legislative branch, sometimes led by a prime minister or president

children.label: government budget
children.description: The proposed expenses and revenues approved by the legislature.

children.label: government employee
children.description: Individuals employed by a government at all levels

children.label: head of government
children.description: The highest official in the executive branch of a political entity

children.label: head of state
children.description: Symbolic or actual chief representative of a nation, such as a monarch, president or emir

children.label: impeachment
children.description: The process of bringing a public official before a tribunal to answer charges of wrongdoing

children.label: legislative body
children.description: A legislature of elected officials representing the people that has the authority to make laws

children.label: lower house (legislature)
children.description: Lower chamber of a legislative body, such as the US House of Representatives or UK House of Commons

children.label: upper house (legislature)
children.description: Senior chamber of a legislative body, such as the US Senate or UK House of Lords

children.label: lobbying
children.description: The attempt by non-government bodies and individuals to affect the outcome of legislation through verbal, or other, persuasion

children.label: local government
children.description: Authorities at borough, city or county level

children.label: minister or secretary (government)
children.description: Senior government official, either elected or appointed, who heads a government department or leads an initiative

children.label: national government
children.description: The ruling body of a nation

children.label: national security
children.description: The protection of a political entity

children.label: armed forces
children.description: The organizations and individuals that serve as part of the military of a political entity

children.label: military service
children.description: Service by an individual in an army or militia. Service may be on a volunteer basis or a result of an involuntary draft or government requirement.

children.label: veterans' affairs
children.description: Care and provision for those who served in the military

children.label: espionage and intelligence
children.description: Covert collection of information

children.label: military weaponry and equipment
children.description: The equipment and weapons used by armed forces and the trade of armaments between political entities

children.label: political committee
children.description: A legislative sub-group that focuses on a specific area or action

children.label: political leadership
children.description: Positions of leadership within political parties and discussion around whether leadership changes need to be made

children.label: political movement and association
children.description: A collective of people with the aim to change government policy or social values in opposition to the status quo

children.label: political party
children.description: Organization that coordinates candidates to run to represent that party in an election

children.label: political party convention
children.description: Meeting of political party to nominate a candidate, choose a party leader or set policy

children.label: political system
children.description: The form of government that is observed, recognised or otherwise declared by a society or state

children.label: absolute monarchy
children.description: Form of government in which a person, who is part of a hereditary line, reigns as head of state for life or until abdication

children.label: communism
children.description: Form of government that aims to replace private property and a profit-based economy with public ownership and communal control of the means of production and the natural resources within in society

children.label: democracy
children.description: Form of government in which the people hold the power, either directly or through elected officials

children.label: democratic socialism
children.description: Form of government that consists of a socialist economy in which the means of production are socially and collectively owned or controlled alongside a democratic political system of government with officials elected to office by citizens

children.label: dictatorship
children.description: Form of government in which a single individual or a small group of individuals hold power without the consent of the people

children.label: theocracy
children.description: Form of government in which authority comes from a religion and the leaders are thought to be divinely guided

children.label: public inquiry
children.description: An official review of events or actions ordered by a government body, including royal commissions

children.label: public officials
children.description: Individuals, usually elected, who are in public service or commonly in the public eye.

children.label: regional government
children.description: Authorities at a level above the local and below the national, such as a state or province

children.label: government policy
children.description: An overall plan or course of action set out by a government intended to influence and guide decisions

children.label: cultural policy
children.description: Government policies related to the promotion and support of the arts

children.label: data protection policy
children.description: Efforts to protect personal information in written, oral or electronic form and regulations around what personal information can be collected by the government or other entities

children.label: economic policy
children.description: Government-directed policy on the economy including, production, taxes and tariffs

children.label: economic development incentive
children.description: The offer of funds, financial incentive programmes or subsidies to stimulate businesses and the economy

children.label: nationalization
children.description: State takeover of private organizations or properties

children.label: privatization
children.description: The transfer of state-owned organizations or properties to private owners

children.label: state-owned enterprise
children.description: Enterprises owned partially or completely by the government

children.label: education policy
children.description: Government programmes and policies related to education, such as the funding of schools and standardized testing

children.label: environmental policy
children.description: Government programs and policies related to environmental issues, such as pollution, renewable energy and conservation

children.label: healthcare policy
children.description: Government programs and policies related to healthcare such as drug policies, psychiatric care, health care funding and pandemic response

children.label: housing and urban planning policy
children.description: Systematic planning of urban and suburban areas and the housing within those areas

children.label: immigration policy
children.description: Policies around immigration into a country such as who may immigrate to a country, how many people are allowed in each year, deportation of illegal immigrants and integration programs that help new immigrants assimilate to a country's culture

children.label: infrastructure policy
children.description: Policies regarding the development and maintenance of the fundamental facilities of a country, city or other area, such as communication, transportation and distribution networks

children.label: local government policy
children.description: Policies for the development and maintenance of a local government area

children.label: nuclear policy
children.description: Government policies around the production of use of nuclear power and weapons

children.label: pension and welfare policy
children.description: Government policies supporting citizens financially through programs such as unemployment payments, pensions and financial support for the poor

children.label: personal weapon control policy
children.description: Government policies and regulations around the personal ownership of firearms and other weapons

children.label: policy towards indigenous people
children.description: Government progams and policies toward indigenous peoples, such as land allocation, rights protection and financial support

children.label: regional development policy
children.description: Government or private policies, such as business incentives, aimed at the development of a region

children.label: regulation of industry
children.description: Government regulation dictating how companies operate

children.label: food and drink regulations
children.description: Government policies relating to the production and selling of food and drink, including ensuring food safety

children.label: sports policies
children.description: Government policies regulating sports, including sports betting, performance enhancing drug laws and the promition of sports to children for health purposes

children.label: taxation policy
children.description: Government programs and policies around the taxation of citizens and entities

children.label: zoning policy
children.description: Polices around the division of land into zones, each of which has a set of regulations for new development

children.label: international relations
children.description: Relations between nations through negotiation, treaty, or diplomacy

children.label: border dispute
children.description: Diplomatic issues between two countries regarding territorial borders

children.label: diplomacy
children.description: Negotiations between representatives of nations or groups of nations and the diplomats who are involved in the talks

children.label: summit meeting
children.description: Meetings between high-level government officials or heads of state for the purpose of diplomatic negotiations to ease international tensions or to discuss common goals

children.label: treaty
children.description: A written agreement between international entities that is binding under international law

children.label: economic sanction
children.description: Economic measures taken by one country or intergovernmental agency against another such as trade restrictions and embargoes

children.label: foreign aid
children.description: Support from one nation to another for purposes such as disaster, general economic development or diplomacy

children.label: international organization
children.description: Organization with members and functions that cross international borders

children.label: refugees and internally displaced people
children.description: People seeking shelter or asylum in another region because of some fear of persecution, conflict, or natural disaster in their own region

children.label: non-governmental organisation (NGO)
children.description: Groups officially outside of government that lobby, demonstrate or campaign on a wide range of issues such as economics, the environment and healthcare

children.label: political prisoners and dissenters
children.description: Individuals who put themselves at risk by expressing their political views and the imprisonment of individuals who speak out against a political authority

roots.label: religion
roots.description: Belief systems, institutions and people who provide moral guidance to followers

children.label: belief systems
children.description: A set of beliefs prescribed by an institution or text often focusing on the worship of a higher power and the outlining of moral guidelines

children.label: Buddhism
children.description: An Asian religion founded in the 6th century BC in India based on the teachings of the Buddha with the goal of overcoming suffering and transcending desire and the individual self to achieve nirvana

children.label: Christianity
children.description: Religions that follow the teachings of Jesus Christ and the Bible

children.label: Catholicism
children.description: Largest Christian religion in the world encompassing the Roman Catholic Church which is led by the pope, and Old Catholicism, a breakaway movement founded in 1870 that denies the dogma of infallibility of the pope

children.label: Christian Orthodoxy
children.description: Eastern rite churches which are characterized by their continuity with the apostolic church, their liturgy and their territorial churches, mainly in eastern and south-eastern Europe and the Middle East

children.label: Mormonism
children.description: Christian religion founded in New York State in the 1820s that follows the teachings of Joseph Smith and the *Book of Mormon*

children.label: Protestantism
children.description: Christian denominations that were formed through the 16th century Reformation movement

children.label: Confucianism
children.description: A system of thought and behavior originating in ancient China and based on the teachings of the philosopher Confucius

children.label: Hinduism
children.description: A religion and social system originating in India that includes a caste system, a belief in reincarnation and the worship of multiple deities

children.label: Islam
children.description: Monotheistic religion that considers Muhammad as a prophet and the Qur'an as holy scripture

children.label: Shia Islam
children.description: The second largest branch of Islam believing that the Prophet Muhammad designated Ali ibn Abi Talib as his successor

children.label: Sunni Islam
children.description: The largest branch of Islam believing that the Prophet Muhammad did not designate a successor

children.label: Jainism
children.description: A religion beginning in the 7th-5th century BC in India that teaches a path to spiritual purity and enlightenment through a disciplined mode of life founded upon the tradition of ahimsa, nonviolence to all living creatures

children.label: Judaism
children.description: A monotheistic religion and culture that follows the teachings of the Torah

children.label: Hasidism
children.description: Jewish religious group that believes that the Torah is the literal word of God and that carrying out this word is what gives meaning and purpose to life

children.label: Scientology
children.description: A set of beliefs and practices invented by American science fiction author L. Ron Hubbard asserting that a human is an immortal, spiritual being (Thetan) that is resident in a physical body

children.label: Shintoism
children.description: An indigenous Japanese polytheistic religion that revolves around kami, supernatural entities believed to inhabit all things

children.label: Sikhism
children.description: An Indian Dharmic religion that originated at the end of the 15th century CE in the Punjab region, developed from the spiritual teachings of Guru Nanak

children.label: Taoism
children.description: A philosophical and spiritual tradition originating in the 4th century BCE in China which emphasizes living in harmony with the Tao, the source, pattern and substance of everything that exists

children.label: Unificationism
children.description: A religion founded in 1954 in South Korea following the teachings of Rev. Syn Myung Moon and known for its mass wedding ceremonies

children.label: Zoroastrianism
children.description: A religion originating in ancient Iran following the teachings of the prophet Zoroaster, predicting the triumph of good over evil and exalting the benevolent deity of wisdom, Ahura Mazda (Wise Lord), as its supreme being

children.label: atheism and agnosticism
children.description: The belief that god does not exist or that it is impossible to know whether a god exists

children.label: cult
children.description: A group that consists of followers who are fully devoted to a charismatic leader. Members are sometimes exploited financially or subject to emotional or physical harm

children.label: nature religion
children.description: Religions that believe nature and the natural world is an embodiment of divinity, sacredness or spiritual power, including indigenous religions practiced in various parts of the world, and modern Pagan faiths, such as Wicca

children.label: relations between religion and government
children.description: Matters arising from the relationship between religions and a government, including the question of whether churches should pay taxes, the push to keep religion out of publicly funded institutions and the freedom, or lack of to wear religious symbols in a school setting

children.label: religious conflict
children.description: Conflicts involving religious differences

children.label: religious facilities
children.description: Any facility where a group carries out its religious rites

children.label: church
children.description: A building used as a place of worship for the Christian religion

children.label: mosque
children.description: A building used as a place of worship for the Islamic religion

children.label: synagogue
children.description: A building used as a place of worship for the Jewish religion

children.label: religious festival and holiday
children.description: Holy day or period of observance in a religion which is sometimes a public holiday

children.label: All Saints Day
children.description: Christian festival celebrated in honor of all the saints, known and unknown. Holiday is also known as All Hallows' Day, Hallowmas, Feast of All Saints or Solemnity of All Saints.

children.label: Christmas
children.description: Christian holiday that celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ. Is also celebrated by many as a secular holiday.

children.label: Easter
children.description: Christian festival commemorating the resurrection of Jesus Christ. Is also celebrated by many as a secular holiday.

children.label: Eid al-Adha
children.description: Muslim festival marking the culmination of the annual hajj pilgrimage and commemorating the willingness of the Prophet Ibrahim to sacrifice his son

children.label: Hanukkah
children.description: Jewish festival, sometimes spelled Chanukah, observed by lighting the candles of a menorah

children.label: Pentecost
children.description: Christian festival, celebrated on the 50th day after Easter commemorating the descent of the Holy Spirit, also known as Whitsun

children.label: Ramadan
children.description: Holy month of fasting in Islam concluding in Eid al-Fitr

children.label: Walpurgis night
children.description: The eve of the Christian feast day of Saint Walpurga, an 8th-century abbess in Francia, celebrated on the night of 30 April and the day of 1 May

children.label: Yom Kippur
children.description: Most solemn of Jewish religious holidays, observed on the 10th day of the lunar month of tishri by fasting and prayer from sunset to sundown the following day

children.label: religious leader
children.description: Person or persons who have a ritual, juridical or otherwise leading role in their respective church or religion

children.label: pope
children.description: Head of the Roman Catholic Church worldwide

children.label: religious ritual
children.description: Established religious rituals such as mass, baptism, prayer meetings and bar and bat mitzvah

children.label: baptism
children.description: A Christian religious rite, sometimes also called a Christening, involving the sprinkling of holy water onto a person's forehead or immersing them in water, symbolizing purification and admission to the Church

children.label: bar and bat mitzvah
children.description: Young person becoming an adult in the Jewish faith

children.label: canonization
children.description: The declaration of a deceased person as an officially recognized saint

children.label: religious text
children.description: Texts regarded as holy or important by a religion

children.label: Bible
children.description: Holy book of Christianity

children.label: Qur'an
children.description: Holy book of Islam

children.label: Torah
children.description: Holy book of Judaism

roots.label: science and technology
roots.description: All aspects pertaining to human understanding of, as well as methodical study and research of natural, formal and social sciences, such as astronomy, linguistics or economics

children.label: biomedical science
children.description: The application of biology-based science to medical fields such as research, health monitoring or medical treatment

children.label: biotechnology
children.description: The scientific manipulation of living organisms and biological processes for scientific, medical or agricultural purposes

children.label: mathematics
children.description: The study of structure, space, change and number in abstract, often using symbolic logic and language, and including subjects such as geometry, algebra or trigonometry

children.label: natural science
children.description: The sciences that deal with matter, energy and the physical world, including physics, biology, chemistry and astronomy

children.label: astronomy
children.description: The study of celestial objects through direct observation and theoretical models

children.label: biology
children.description: The study of the anatomy, behavior, origin, physiology and other aspects of living organisms

children.label: botany
children.description: The study of the physical and physiological structure, genetics, ecology and other aspects of plants

children.label: genetics
children.description: The study of genes in living organisms, and of their role in heredity, development or genetic adaptation

children.label: paleontology
children.description: The study of prehistoric life forms, geological periods and fossils

children.label: physiology
children.description: The study of the vital processes, internal organs or functional mechanisms of living organisms

children.label: zoology
children.description: The study of the biology, physiology, development, behavior or other aspects of animals

children.label: chemistry
children.description: The study of the composition and properties of matter on the scale of atoms and molecules, and of the reactions between compounds

children.label: cosmology
children.description: The study of the origin, evolution, organization and structure of the universe

children.label: geology
children.description: The study of Earth's physical processes, material structures and its properties

children.label: horticulture
children.description: The study and art of plant cultivation, including landscape and garden design and plant conservation

children.label: marine science
children.description: The study of living organisms and environments in saltwater ecosystems

children.label: meteorology
children.description: The study of atmospheric chemistry and physics, with a focus on weather forecasting

children.label: physics
children.description: The study of the movement and structure of matter, and how it relates to energy

children.label: electromagnetism
children.description: The study of the physical interactions between electrically charged particles and magnetic fields

children.label: nuclear physics
children.description: The study of the structure and behavior of atomic nuclei

children.label: particle physics
children.description: The study of the nature, properties and interactions of the elementary particles that constitute matter

children.label: scientific institution
children.description: Institution that carries out or governs scientific work, such as the National Academy of Arts and Sciences

children.label: scientific research
children.description: The scientific and methodical investigation of events, procedures and interactions to explain why they occur, or to find solutions for problems

children.label: medical research
children.description: Investigation conducted in the fields of health and medicine, such as genetic studies, disease research or pharmaceutical drug trials

children.label: scientific exploration
children.description: Land, sea or space journeys undertaken to discover new information

children.label: space exploration
children.description: The scientific exploration of outer space through manned and unmanned missions

children.label: scientific innovation
children.description: The development or creation of new scientific or technological products or processes, such as biotech or artificial intelligence applications, robotic limbs or nanoscale cameras

children.label: scientific publication
children.description: Academic research findings published in a journal, book or thesis

children.label: scientific standards
children.description: Nationally or internationally established rules governing scientific and technological study and development, such as calibration standards for scientific tools or equipment

children.label: social sciences
children.description: The study of human society in such aspects as linguistics, anthropology, economics or sociology

children.label: anthropology
children.description: The study of human behavior and social interactions across time

children.label: archeology
children.description: The study of human activity throughout time and cultural history, using artefacts left behind by ancient peoples

children.label: economics
children.description: The study of the laws and principles of economies, such as the production and distribution of goods and services

children.label: geography
children.description: The study of the physical features of the surface of Earth and its political divisions

children.label: history
children.description: The study of human events of the past

children.label: information science
children.description: The study and practice of collecting, classifying, storing, retrieving and disseminating information

children.label: linguistics
children.description: The study of all aspects of human language such as syntax, phonetics, written and spoken forms and variations over time

children.label: philosophy
children.description: The study of the principles and fundamental questions about matters such as the mind, reason, morality or values

children.label: political science
children.description: The study of the principles of political and governmental systems, political thought and practices

children.label: psychology
children.description: The study of the human mind, mental characteristics and emotional processes

children.label: sociology
children.description: The study of human social organization, social relationships and societal changes

children.label: study of law
children.description: The study of legal systems and the philosophy of law

children.label: technology and engineering
children.description: The study and practice of industrial or applied sciences such as physics, hydrodynamics or thermodynamics

children.label: aerospace engineering
children.description: The study, design, development and construction of aircraft, spacecraft and missile systems

children.label: rocketry
children.description: The study, design, development and construction of rockets

children.label: agricultural technology
children.description: The study and development of techniques and machinery to improve agricultural management and productivity

children.label: civil engineering
children.description: The study, design, development and construction of structures such as buildings, bridges, tunnels, irrigation and sewage systems, streets or railroads

children.label: electronic engineering
children.description: The study, design, development and application of systems built on the exchange of electrical charges, such as consumer devices, communications systems or industrial computers

children.label: identification technology
children.description: The study, development, application and ethical considerations of technological methods for identifying products, animals or people; including radio frequency, biometrics or face recognition

children.label: information technology and computer science
children.description: The study and design of computer systems, software and networks

children.label: artificial intelligence
children.description: An attempt to let computers simulate how the human brain works by applying statistical, heuristic or machine learning methods and algorithms to large datasets. Enables a long range of automatic functions like image recognition and categorization.

children.label: materials science
children.description: The study of the composition, structure and properties of materials for their use in industry and manufacturing

children.label: mechanical engineering
children.description: The study and application of the design, construction and operation of mechanical systems

children.label: micro science
children.description: The study of and technologies built at a microscopic scale, such as microbiology or microcomputing

children.label: nanotechnology
children.description: Manipulating objects at the molecular scale

roots.label: society
roots.description: The concerns, issues, affairs and institutions relevant to human social interactions, problems and welfare, such as poverty, human rights and family planning

children.label: communities
children.description: A group of individuals actively sharing a common value or interest

children.label: fraternal and community group
children.description: Social organizations whose members freely associate for a mutually beneficial purpose such as for social, professional or honorary principles. Groups include Rotary clubs, Lions clubs or Freemasons.

children.label: social networking
children.description: Social interactions, either in person or online, intended to share information and build relationships around common interests

children.label: demographic group
children.description: A subset of society with shared traits

children.label: LGBTQ
children.description: People who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer

children.label: adults
children.description: People above an age set by law that entitles them to full liability and certain privileges such as the legal right to drink alcoholic beverages and to vote

children.label: children
children.description: Young people, usually pre-pubescent, who are legally considered minors and are in a guardianship relationship with adults

children.label: disabilities
children.description: Physical or mental conditions that limit a person's movements, senses, or activities

children.label: gender
children.description: The classification of individuals as male, female, or a non-binary designation

children.label: indigenous people
children.description: People who are the original owners and caretakers of a given region, also known as native peoples, first peoples or aboriginal peoples, in contrast to groups that have settled, occupied or colonized the area more recently

children.label: infants
children.description: Very young people, usually defined as being just born up to the age of two

children.label: men
children.description: People who identify as male, focusing on the group as a demographic, and masculinity

children.label: national or ethnic minority
children.description: Groups of people that form a minority on an ethnic or national basis, and their status or issues relating to the majority

children.label: senior citizens
children.description: People having passed the age of retirement

children.label: teenagers
children.description: Young people between the ages that describe childhood and adulthood

children.label: women
children.description: People who identify as female, focusing on the group as a demographic, and accomplishments, such as the first woman to achieve a milestone or serve in a role

children.label: demographics
children.description: The study of human populations and their characteristics, for example statistics or trends around aging populations in a particular geographic region

children.label: population and census
children.description: The official count of people living in a given geopolitical area, usually carried out by a governmental body

children.label: discrimination
children.description: Unfair treatment of, or policies or practices against, individuals or groups of people on the basis of real or perceived membership in a group, such as race, sexual orientation, political or religious beliefs, age or height

children.label: ageism
children.description: Discrimination against individuals or groups of people on the basis of age

children.label: racism
children.description: Discrimination against individuals or groups of people on the basis of race

children.label: religious discrimination
children.description: Unfair treatment of individuals or groups of people on the basis of their religious belief

children.label: sexism
children.description: Discrimination against individuals or groups of people, usually women, on the basis of gender

children.label: diversity, equity and inclusion
children.description: Efforts that seeks to promote the fair treatment and full participation of groups of people who have historically been underrepresented or subject to discrimination on the basis of identity or disability

children.label: emigration
children.description: Leaving one's country of residence to settle permanently elsewhere

children.label: family
children.description: A group of people related genetically or by a legal bond, or who consider themselves part of a familial unit regardless of genetic or legal status

children.label: Dating and Relationships
children.description: The development of an intimate connection between individuals, through various forms of activities enjoyed together, often leading to a legal or permanent union such as marriage

children.label: adoption
children.description: The legal process of transferring parental rights to someone other than a person's birth parents, that person usually being a child

children.label: divorce
children.description: The process by which a marriage is legally dissolved

children.label: family planning
children.description: Services and education aimed at informing individual decisions about reproduction, such as fertility, in vitro fertilisation, contraception or abortion

children.label: abortion
children.description: The intentional termination of a pregnancy for elective or medical reasons

children.label: contraception
children.description: A method or device used to prevent pregnancy

children.label: marriage
children.description: The legal or socially recognized union of individuals, which establishes rights and obligations between them

children.label: parenting
children.description: The caring for and support of a child's physical, emotional, developmental and social needs from birth to adulthood

children.label: pregnancy and childbirth
children.description: Social and medical issues around pregnancy and giving birth including, doulas and midwives, obstetrics and medical concerns

children.label: fundamental rights
children.description: The political, social, cultural and economic rights to which all people are entitled, usually upheld by law

children.label: censorship and freedom of speech
children.description: The right to express opinions without restraint and attempts to supress speech by an organization or individual

children.label: civil rights
children.description: Guarantees of protection to individuals  freedom from violation by governments, political and social organizations, and other individuals as determined by the laws or constitutions of an individual country

children.label: freedom of religion
children.description: The right to practice the religion of one's choosing and efforts to violate this right through the intimidation of believers or laws that encroach on religious rituals

children.label: freedom of the press
children.description: The right of the press to report on stories freely and efforts by governments, organizations or individuals to suppress, jail or kill journalists who are reporting the news

children.label: human rights
children.description: Rights entitled to be enjoyed by all people universally

children.label: privacy
children.description: The right of an individual or group to keep information about themselves private

children.label: women's rights
children.description: The rights of women to be treated equally as men, such as pay parity, feminism and bodily autonomy around abortion

children.label: immigration
children.description: The movement of individuals or groups of people from one country to another

children.label: illegal immigration
children.description: The movement of individuals or groups of people from one country to another without legal authorization from the destination country

children.label: social condition
children.description: The circumstances or state of affairs affecting a person's life, welfare and relations with others in a society

children.label: homelessness
children.description: The social condition defined by lack of permanent residence, living in shelters or on streets, and the issues and problems associated with it

children.label: poverty
children.description: The lack of sufficient resources and means to provide basic needs such as food, clothing or shelter for oneself and one's family

children.label: social problem
children.description: Issues related to human rights, human welfare and other areas of societal concern

children.label: abusive behavior
children.description: Actions that intentionally harm another person or people, often on an ongoing basis, such as psychological or mental abuse, negligence, physical or sexual abuse and torture

children.label: addiction
children.description: The habitual and compulsive use of substances such as alcohol or drugs, or behavior such as gambling, gaming or sex, often causing detrimental effects on the body, brain, and relationships with others

children.label: bullying
children.description: Taking actions meant to harm, coerce and intimidate another person perceived as vulnerable. These actions can be taken in person or online.

children.label: juvenile delinquency
children.description: Unlawful conduct perpetrated by minors, often on a repeated basis

children.label: prostitution
children.description: The business of engaging in sexual activity in exchange for payment

children.label: sexual misconduct
children.description: Unwanted behavior of a sexual nature that is of lesser offense than felony sexual assault, particularly when behavior occurs in a normally non-sexual situation, or where there is some aspect of personal power or authority involved

children.label: slavery
children.description: The ownership of people as property, and the involuntary servitude of those people to their owners, which includes unpaid labor and coerced actions

children.label: values
children.description: A person's or group's principles or standards of behavior, which guide their way of living and choices made

children.label: death and dying
children.description: Social, medical and mental health issues relating to people at the end of their lives

children.label: euthanasia
children.description: The practice of humanely ending the life of a person suffering from a terminal illness

children.label: assisted suicide
children.description: The practice of assisting a person suffering from a terminal illness in the process of suicide, often with a physician's oversight

children.label: suicide
children.description: The intentional taking of one's own life

children.label: ethics
children.description: The moral values and standards that define right and wrong actions or decisions

children.label: pornography
children.description: The depiction of sexually explicit acts in various media renditions, such as video or photos, often considered obscene or immoral

children.label: sexual behavior
children.description: The manner in which people express their sexuality in physical acts

children.label: welfare
children.description: Help for those in need of food, housing, health and other services

children.label: charity
children.description: The voluntary giving of money, food or other necessities to those in need

children.label: child care
children.description: Services and facilities that look after children while their parents are working or away, including daycare centers and programs

children.label: elderly care
children.description: The long-term care of the elderly provided by residential institutions or by paid daily help in the home

children.label: long-term care
children.description: Services provided on an extended and ongoing basis to patients suffering from chronic illness or disability

children.label: public housing
children.description: Housing that is owned or managed by a government or nonprofit organization and rented to tenants with the aim of making housing affordable. Eligibility for such housing arrangements varies country to country.

children.label: social services
children.description: Social programs, usually publicly sponsored, aimed at promoting people's welfare, such as housing, health care or education services

roots.label: sport
roots.description: Competitive activity or skill that involves physical and/or mental effort and organizations and bodies involved in these activities

children.label: competition discipline
children.description: Different types of sport which can be executed in competitions

children.label: 3x3 basketball
children.description: A variation of basketball played three a side on one basketball hoop

children.label: American football
children.description: Team ball game that opposes two teams of 11 that have offense and defense sections. Each offense attempts to move an oval ball down the 120 yards long field. Points are scored by advancing the ball into the opposing team*s end zone.

children.label: Australian rules football
children.description: A form of football played by two teams of 18 competing on a pitch by running with and passing an oval ball. Points are scored by moving the ball between goal posts. Governed by the Australian Football League.

children.label: Canadian football
children.description: Team ball game that opposes two teams of 12 that have offense and defense sections. Each offense attempts to move an oval ball down the 150 yards long field. Points are scored by advancing the ball into the opposing team*s end zone.

children.label: Gaelic football
children.description: A form of football played by two teams of 15 competing on a pitch by running with, kicking and passing a spherical ball. Points are scored by moving the ball between goal posts. Governed by the Gaelic Athletic Association.

children.label: Jai Alai (Pelota)
children.description: A fast ball play using either the bare hand or a wicker scoop in an arena of walls of different outlay and size

children.label: archery
children.description: Archers use bows and arrows to aim at targets 1.22 meters in diameter which are on average 70 meters distant.

children.label: crossbow shooting
children.description: Shooting with crossbow on targets from different distances

children.label: longbow
children.description: Shooting with longbow on targets from different distances. The competition is held outdoors on an open (flat) field.

children.label: arm wrestling
children.description: A form of wrestling in which two participants grapple arm-to-arm

children.label: synchronized swimming
children.description: A sport in which swimmers, in solo, duet or team configurations, perform coordinated or identical movements in time to music. They are judged and are awarded points for body position, control, and the degree of difficulty of the moves.

children.label: synchronized free routine
children.description: In the free program, music, movements and their order of execution are not restricted.

children.label: synchronized technical routine
children.description: Contestants obtain points from 10 sitting judges by executing certain synchronized artistic shapes and movements in the water. In the technical program, competitors must execute a range of specific moves in a given order.

children.label: track and field
children.description: Competitions involving foot races, jumping and throwing which can be on a track inside a stadium or on outside roads

children.label: cross-country run
children.description: Competitors run over rough ground and not on a track

children.label: decathlon
children.description: Individual men's competition which involves accumulating points in 10 different disciplines over two days: 1st day - 100m, long-jump, shot-putt, high-jump, 400m. 2nd day - 110m hurdles, discus, pole-vault, javelin and 1,500 meters.

children.label: discus throw
children.description: Competitors stand in a netted circle with a 2.50 meters diameter and with a turning motion attempt to throw a discus weighing 2kg for men and 1kg for women as far as possible

children.label: hammer throw
children.description: Competitors throw a hammer consisting of a metal ball, chain and handle as far as they can from a netted circle which is 2.13 meters in diameter. The hammer weighs 7.26kg for men and 4kg for women

children.label: heptathlon
children.description: Competition involving seven separate disciplines over two days. 1st day - 100m hurdles, high jump, shot put, 200 meters. 2nd day - long-jump, javelin, 800 meters

children.label: high jump
children.description: Competitors build up speed over a short sprint and then jump as high as possible over a horizontal bar

children.label: hurdles
children.description: A sprint running race where athletes jump over a series of upright frames

children.label: javelin throw
children.description: Competitors in a specially-designated throwing area attempt to fling a spear-like javelin as far as possible. The javelin weighs 800 grams for men and 600 grams for women.

children.label: long distance run
children.description: A running race at distances for more than 1500 meters

children.label: long jump
children.description: Competitors build up speed over a short sprint and then jump in one leap as far as possible

children.label: middle distance run
children.description: A running race at distances for more than 400 meters and up to and including 1500 meters

children.label: pentathlon
children.description: Only indoor, 60m hurdles, high jump, shot put, long jump, 800 m

children.label: pole vault
children.description: Competitors use a flexible pole to propel themselves feet-first into the air and clear a bar which is raised higher at each round of jumps.

children.label: race walking
children.description: A race requiring the competitor to have always one foot on the ground

children.label: relay run
children.description: A team of athletes run a relay over identical distances

children.label: shot put
children.description: Competitors stand in a circle with a 2.13 meters diameter and attempt to throw a metal ball weighing 7.26 kg for men and 4kg for women as far as possible. The longest throw wins.

children.label: sprint run
children.description: A running race at distances of up to and including 400 meters

children.label: steeplechase (athletics)
children.description: Obstacle race in athletics including barriers and water jumps

children.label: triple jump
children.description: Competitors build up speed over a short sprint and then attempt to jump as far forward as they can using a hop, skip and a jump technique.

children.label: badminton
children.description: Two players or two teams of two compete by hitting a shuttlecock weighing approximately five grams over a high net. The aim for each player/team is to prevent the shuttlecock landing on their side of the court.

children.label: bandy
children.description: Played outdoors on ice. The size of the ice rink is about the size of a soccer field. Skates like ice hockey. A small hard ball is used for playing. Players play with sticks, much like in ice hockey, but the sticks are shorter and more rounded than in ice

children.label: baseball
children.description: A game between two teams of nine played on an enclosed ground. The team which scores the most points wins. A point is scored when a player runs around the ground marked out by four bases. To do this he has to hit the ball thrown at him by a rival player.

children.label: rubberball baseball
children.description: Sometimes called ''soft baseball,'' the game is played with a rubber baseball of varying degrees of hardness depending upon the age and level of the players.

children.label: basketball
children.description: Game played between two teams of five - points are scored by placing the large inflated ball into a net fixed on a ring 3.05m above the ground.

children.label: biathlon
children.description: A combination of cross-country skiing and target shooting on a 12.5 K course in a pursuit format.

children.label: billiards
children.description: A cue sport with balls on a table without a specific order to play them

children.label: bobsleigh
children.description: One, two or four people racing down a course in a sled that consists of a main hull, a frame, two axles and sets of runners. The total time of all heats in a competition is added together to determine the winner.

children.label: bodybuilding
children.description: Competitions where participants perform specific poses to display their muscles that have been strengthened and enlarged through strenuous exercise. Competitors are judged based on criteria such as symmetry, muscularity and conditioning.

children.label: boules
children.description: Collective name of a number of games where the common goal is to move the competitor's balls as close to a small target ball as possible, played on a grass or sand surface. Balls are thrown (as in petanque and boules) or rolled (as in lawn bowls or bocce).

children.label: boxing
children.description: Combat sport in which two men/women fight using only their fists covered by padded gloves in a square ring measuring 6m a side. The fight is usually split into 12 rounds of three minutes each.

children.label: bullfighting
children.description: Classical contest pitting man against the bull

children.label: canoe slalom
children.description: Competitors navigate a canoe or a kayak on a white-water course, passing through a combination of upstream and downstream gates on river rapids in the fastest time possible

children.label: canoe sprint
children.description: Taking place on a flatwater course, multiple canoes take off at once and race each other to the finish

children.label: canoeing
children.description: Competition involving canoes which are generally kneeled and paddled with a single-bladed paddle

children.label: casting (fishing)
children.description: Using fishing equipment to hit a target and score points

children.label: cheerleading
children.description: Cheer squads competing against each other to perform a routine that includes stunts, jumps and tumbling set to music. Squads are judged on difficulty and execution.

children.label: chess
children.description: Competition between two players using a checkered board with 16 pieces to each side, each with specific ranges of movement depending on their identity

children.label: competitive dancing
children.description: Dancing competition where competitors are judged on technique and interpretation.

children.label: breaking (breakdance)
children.description: Dancing competition featuring an urban dance style that originated in the United States in the 1970s with roots in hip-hop culture and characterized by acrobatic movements, stylized footwork, and the key role played by the DJ and the MC during battles

children.label: cricket
children.description: Ball sport involving two teams of 11 players, balls, bats and wickets. The aim is to score as many runs as possible, and to get the opposing team 'out'. A 'run' involves a player running between two wickets. The opposing team try to get their rivals 'out'

children.label: croquet
children.description: Using mallets to hit a ball through hoops

children.label: curling
children.description: A game played on ice with large flat round stones. A player throws the stone, aiming at a target. Teammates of the player who has thrown the stone can sweep the ice in front of the stone to help smooth its path towards the target.

children.label: icestock sport
children.description: Similar to curling, played on targets on ice, different stones with straight handle and different rules, played in alpine countries

children.label: cycling
children.description: A race over a given distance on bicycles.

children.label: artistic cycling
children.description: Individual or teams on one or two bicycles in an arena. Points are awarded by a jury.

children.label: bmx freestyle
children.description: Riders are given a fixed time to perform acrobatics tricks and skills, with tricks scored on multiple aspects including difficulty, originality, execution, height and creativity

children.label: bmx racing
children.description: Bicycle racing in with inline start and various obstacles over off-road circuits.

children.label: cycle ball
children.description: Competitive team sport using bicycles. One team against another with two persons per team. The aim is for competitors to move the ball using the front and rear wheels without letting their feet touch the ground.

children.label: mountain biking
children.description: All-terrain, off-road bicycle riding requiring endurance and specially adapted mountain bikes

children.label: darts
children.description: The sport in which small darts are thrown at a dartboard, a circular target divided into numbered sections.

children.label: diving
children.description: Competitors dive off a fixed or spring board and are assessed by seven judges giving marks up to ten for their acrobatic moves.

children.label: platform diving
children.description: Divers take off from a high platform

children.label: springboard diving
children.description: Divers dive from a high springboard.

children.label: synchronized diving
children.description: Two competitors from the same team dive off at the same time from separate platforms or springboards. As well as being judged on the standard criteria they are also awarded marks for synchronization.

children.label: dog racing
children.description: Dogs racing around a track

children.label: duathlon
children.description: An athletic event involving running and cycling

children.label: eSports
children.description: Competitions involving video games played by professional gamers

children.label: equestrian
children.description: Horse-based sport disciplines governed by the International Federation for Equestrian Sports, such as dressage, eventing, show jumping and vaulting

children.label: fencing
children.description: Combat sport using a sword or foil.

children.label: field hockey
children.description: A ball sport involving two teams of 11 players using curved sticks. The aim is to score as many goals as possible.

children.label: figure skating
children.description: To obtain the best marks possible from nine judges who award scores after two prepared sections - both skated to music - during which competitors must attempt to achieve the greatest possible harmony between artistic flair and technical precision.

children.label: fist ball
children.description: Men's team sport similar to volleyball (with a much lower net) executed mainly in gymnastics clubs

children.label: floorball
children.description: Played indoors in a court the size of a basketball court. 6 players per team, of which one is a goalkeeper. He/she operates kneeling but there is no goal-stick like in ice hockey. The players use plastic clubs and a light plastic ball to pass and shot goal

children.label: flying disc
children.description: A group of events all played with a flying plastic disc. The exact regulation for the disc is different in different events but it has to be unbroken of solid plastic and a production model with no modification. Flying disc is sometimes called Frisbee.

children.label: soccer
children.description: A form of football played by two teams competing on a pitch by kicking a spherical ball. Points are scored by kicking or heading the ball into a goal. Governed by the Fédération Internationale de Football Association

children.label: beach soccer
children.description: A soccer-based game played on sand with five players per team

children.label: futsal
children.description: A soccer-based game played indoors on a hard court with five players per team

children.label: football 5-a-side
children.description: A variation of association football in which each team fields five players and play is on a smaller pitch. An official Summer Paralympics sport.

children.label: goalball
children.description: A team sport for athletes with a vision impairment, using a ball containing bells

children.label: golf
children.description: A game to hit a small hard ball with different clubs around a course of typically 18 holes varying in distance and during a round. The object, depending on the scoring formulae, is to make the fewest strokes possible

children.label: mini golf
children.description: A game where small hard balls must be holed on an artificial course in as few strokes from the club as possible

children.label: gymnastics
children.description: A sport consisting of a variety of disciplines in which gymnasts perform artistic and acrobatic moves using different apparatus.

children.label: artistic gymnastics
children.description: Gymnasts perform artistic and acrobatic moves on different apparatus. There are 6 events for men and 4 for women

children.label: rhythmic gymnastics
children.description: Mixture of dance and gymnastic moves

children.label: trampoline
children.description: Competitors perform complicated twists and turns while bouncing on the trampoline.

children.label: handball (team)
children.description: A ball game using the hands contested by two teams of seven trying to throw the ball into the opponents goal.

children.label: hornuss
children.description: Swiss team sport with 16 or 18 men per team. A rubber puck is hit towards the field of the adversary team which tries to hit the puck in the air with a wooden board thrown in the air

children.label: horse racing
children.description: Mounted horse races.

children.label: hurling
children.description: A game played by two teams of fifteen each with a curved wooden stick called a hurley. The object is to score a goal by hitting the small ball between the opponents' goalposts either over the crossbar or under it into a net guarded by a goalkeeper.

children.label: ice hockey
children.description: Two teams of six heavily padded skaters try and outscore each other by hitting a puck into the opponents goal.

children.label: sledge hockey
children.description: Like ice hockey but instead of skates small sledges are used. Competitors move by pushing with the arms

children.label: kabaddi
children.description: The attacking side scores by touching, and the side to guard scores by capturing. The attacker continues calling it 'kabaddi'.

children.label: kayaking
children.description: Competition involving kayaks where the paddler sits with their legs facing forward using a double-bladed paddle

children.label: kiting
children.description: Action sport where a person harnesses the power of the wind to propel themselves across water, land or snow on a board, snowboard or skis. Variations of the sport are called kiteboarding/kitesurfing, snowkiting or landkiting.

children.label: lacrosse
children.description: Two teams of helmeted and padded players try and outscore each other using a netted stick and hard ball.

children.label: luge
children.description: Luge (French word for sled) is competed in singles or doubles. The competitor(s) lay on their back on an open sled and race down a course. The competitor(s) and the sled must be in contact when passing the finishing line. The competitor can steer the sled

children.label: marathon
children.description: A road race where competitors run 42.195km, generally through city streets

children.label: martial arts
children.description: Martial arts are codified systems and traditions of combat practices, which are practiced for a variety of reasons: self-defense, competition, physical health and fitness, entertainment, as well as mental, physical, and spiritual development.

children.label: Taekwon-Do
children.description: A martial art of Korean origin

children.label: judo
children.description: A defensive martial art.

children.label: jukendo
children.description: Japanese traditional martial art using a model rifle made of wood. 'Juken' means a rifle or gun with blade (bayonet)

children.label: karate
children.description: A martial art where chops, punches, kicks and throws are used to defeat an opponent.

children.label: kendo
children.description: Japanese traditional martial art using a bamboo sword, sometimes called Japanese fencing

children.label: kickboxing
children.description: Stand-up combat sport based on kicking and punching an opponent

children.label: krav maga
children.description: Fighting and self-defense sport that combines elements from aikido, boxing, judo, karate and wrestling

children.label: kyudo
children.description: Japanese traditional martial art using a bamboo bow and arrows, sometimes called Japanese archery

children.label: mixed martial arts
children.description: A full-contact combat sport using techniques from various combat sports and martial arts

children.label: naginata
children.description: Japanese traditional martial art using a pole sword made of wood. 'Naginata' means a spear with a curved blade

children.label: sombo (martial art)
children.description: Style of martial art originating in the Soviet Union that is recognized as a form of amateur wrestling

children.label: wushu
children.description: Chinese traditional martial art

children.label: modern pentathlon
children.description: The Modern Pentathlon comprises five events run over a single day in the following order: shooting, fencing, swimming, horse riding and running.

children.label: motor car racing
children.description: Racing with cars

children.label: motorboat racing
children.description: Racing with boats with engines

children.label: motorcycling
children.description: Races with 2, 3 or 4 wheels vehicles with a saddle and handlebars

children.label: mountain climbing
children.description: Moving up mountains using hands and feet

children.label: ice climbing
children.description: Climbing of ice features such as icefalls and frozen cliffs

children.label: mountaineering
children.description: Competitive alpine climbing

children.label: netball
children.description: A woman's sport similar to basketball though without a board behind the basket

children.label: orienteering
children.description: An individual time-trial over a route marked out by beacons. The competitor has to search out and find in a specific order. The contestant makes his way with the help of a compass and map

children.label: ski orienteering

children.label: rugby union

children.label: grass skiing

children.label: stand up paddleboarding (SUP)

children.label: sumo wrestling

children.label: tennis

children.label: track cycling

children.label: triathlon
children.description: An endurance multi-sport where competitors first swim, then cycle and then run a road race. Distances vary according to the competition.

children.label: tug-of-war
children.description: Two teams pulling against each other on a rope

children.label: underwater sports

children.label: volleyball
children.description: Two teams of six record points by hitting a ball over a net into the opponent's half of the court, keeping it in the air at all times. Points are won when opponents fail to return the ball.

children.label: beach volleyball
children.description: Two teams of two players compete on a sand court. Unlike indoor volleyball, points are scored only when the serving team wins a rally or forces an error. The sand surface makes it more physically demanding than volleyball

children.label: water polo
children.description: Played in a pool between two teams of 7, who must stay afloat and can only use one hand to pass the ball or swim with it before trying to throw it into the opponents net to score goals.

children.label: water skiing

children.label: weightlifting and powerlifting

children.label: sports medal and trophy

children.label: sports record

children.label: sport event

children.label: Olympic Games

children.label: Paralympic Games

children.label: final game
children.description: Single game that determines the winner of a championship, such as the Super Bowl or Champions League Final

children.label: playoff championship
children.description: A competitive tournament, often played after the regular season of a sports league by the top competitors to determine the league champion or a similar accolade. Can also apply to an all-in elimination tournament meant to produce a final champion.

children.label: regular competition

children.label: sport industry
children.description: Commercial issues related to sport

children.label: sport organization
children.description: Organizations or associations that govern sports

children.label: sport venue
children.description: Commercial facility for sporting event

children.label: sports management and ownership

children.label: sports officiating
children.description: Referees, umpires and other staff who enforce the rules of a sport from on the field of play

children.label: sports transaction
children.description: The transfer of an athlete from one team to another, the hiring or drafting of an athlete onto a team or the change in professional status of a player on a team

children.description: The long- or short-term meteorological prediction and reporting of the upcoming weather for a given region

children.label: weather statistic
children.description: Numerical facts about the weather such as temperature, barometric pressure, river levels, humidity or high and low tides

children.label: weather warning
